dedupe_keys.name: real time validation of false data injection identification in active distribution systems

description: The documented application tests a false-data identification method using an OPAL-RT hardware-in-the-loop replica and a scaled-down power-system testbed of a Greek active distribution system with nine PV plants. The authors report all 378 tested attacks detected across simple and sophisticated, single-snapshot and daily-series scenarios with different power factors. This bounded experimental outcome does not establish field readiness or universal detection. Its nine-plant description differs from the 16-plant pilot and nine-node equivalent described in the related energy-community dataset; exact experiment overlap is not assumed. The source authors provide the native description and file descriptors through Zenodo. Only metadata was inspected; no measurements, archives, source code or document bodies were retrieved. Public access and the deposit document licence do not establish executable access, software reuse rights or operating costs. Coverage remains bounded to the named experiments, with other geographic and temporal fields unknown. Related project resources may overlap; common project membership does not establish identical simulation inputs or results.
name: Real-Time Validation of False Data Injection Identification in Active Distribution Systems
notes: Native publication date is not a verified observation interval. Project membership alone does not establish resource inclusion. Listed unverified routes timed out in zero-body landing checks; exact native metadata was retrieved successfully. Underlying files remain unchecked.
outcomes: Source-defined findings and limits are stated in the description.
